subject: Next steps: PoC deployment mode & trial plan — Acme Corp
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lane <jordan.lane@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & PoC plan options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment before we draft a formal PoC: 

- Workload: low-latency customer-facing chat + nightly batch embeddings for search reindexing. Estimate: ~50 req/s peak, mostly short prompts.
- Key constraints: data isolation and SSO (SAML), predictable latency during peak, and a hard requirement for encryption-at-rest with keys you control.
- Deployment modes we discussed: Hosted API (fastest to start), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput + isolation), Private VPC/on-prem (for ultimate data control).

From our call, it sounded like Dedicated capacity is likely the best fit given throughput and isolation needs, but you asked for a plan that lets you validate both performance and the controls (KMS integration, audit logs) before committing.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben/Redwood to send a 3-week PoC scope (success criteria, test plan, timeline, resources) — attachment: PoC-scope.xlsx
2) Customer to confirm stakeholders (ML Platform, Security, Procurement) and target dates for pilot -> production
3) Kickoff meeting to align on test data, test harness, and access (we can provide ephemeral tokens or VPN/peering for Dedicated)

Can you confirm the stakeholders and whether the suggested 3-week PoC window (target kickoff week of May 25) works for your team?

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148

From: Jordan Lane <jordan.lane@acmecorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>, Tammy Novak <t.novak@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & PoC plan options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Ben —

Thanks for the clear notes. Confirming our preferences and stakeholders: 

- Deployment preference: Dedicated capacity as primary. We want predictable throughput and isolation; fallback to Hosted API for burst traffic is acceptable as a contingency. Private VPC/on-prem is not our preferred path for this PoC due to time/ops constraints, but we may revisit for a later phase.
- Stakeholders: Jordan Lane (ML Platform), Tammy Novak (Security), Procurement (procurement@acmecorp.com). I can loop in our SRE lead after kickoff if needed.
- Timeline: pilot target week June 14 (pilot run for ~2 weeks), production rollout target mid-July. We can accelerate kickoff earlier if Redwood can provide a one-page security checklist and the PoC scope by EOD Monday.

Please proceed with the PoC scope and include success criteria around latency (p95), throughput, and KMS integration verification.

Jordan
Jordan Lane
Director, ML Platform | Acme Corp

Marissa / Rachel —

Forwarding Jordan's reply. TL;DR: Dedicated preferred, fallback to hosted for bursts, pilot target mid-June. Jordan asked for a one-page security checklist and the PoC scope by EOD Monday.

Action items: 
- Marissa: can you draft the 3-week PoC plan (scope + test harness + success criteria) and the one-page security checklist for Tammy? Attach a test harness template and rough resource estimate (GPU counts / node sizes).
- Rachel: can you flag any known constraints on dedicated capacity availability w/our infra team and estimated cost range for the pilot so we can give Acme an estimate?

Proposed kickoff: Wed, May 27, 10am PT — does that work for you both?

Thanks,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up & PoC plan options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Ben / Rachel —

I can take point on the PoC. Attached is a draft PoC-plan.pdf (high level) and I'll convert the PoC-scope.xlsx Ben referenced into a runbook and test checklist. Highlights: 

Success criteria (examples):
- Latency: p95 user request latency < 200ms under representative load
- Throughput: sustain 50 req/s for 10 minutes with <1% error rate
- Functional: embedding quality parity within 5% measured by internal eval set
- Security/compliance: KMS key rotation + audit log ingestion verified; SAML SSO test pass; no raw transcript retention beyond agreed TTL

Timeline:
- Week 0 (kickoff 27 May): environment setup (Dedicated pool), access + secret exchange, baseline tests
- Week 1: performance tuning, KV/cache warm-up, scripted load tests
- Week 2: customer validation tests, security checklist verification, final handoff prep

Stakeholders: Marissa Cole (PoC owner, Redwood), Jordan Lane (Acme ML Platform), Tammy Novak (Acme Security), Procurement (contracting).

I'll have the full runbook + one-page security checklist ready by EOD Monday and can present the plan at kickoff. If the customer wants earlier pilot dates, we can compress to a 2-week runway but will need immediate SRE time.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
